source_caption:
🎬 Unstoppable (2010)

Unstoppable follows two railroad workers who find themselves in a desperate race against time when an unmanned freight train carrying hazardous chemicals begins speeding uncontrollably through Pennsylvania. Veteran engineer Frank Barnes and rookie conductor Will Colson are working an ordinary shift when they learn that a massive locomotive has escaped control and is rapidly approaching populated areas. With the runaway train gaining speed and threatening to cause a catastrophic disaster, railroad officials scramble to find a way to stop it before innocent lives are lost. As several attempts to derail or slow the train fail, Frank realizes that he and Will may be the only people capable of preventing tragedy. Despite their differences in experience and personality, the two men must put aside their disagreements and work together to carry out an extremely dangerous plan. Meanwhile, rail yard supervisor Connie Hooper coordinates emergency efforts while facing pressure from company executives more concerned with protecting their financial interests. As the runaway train races toward a dangerous curve near a heavily populated city, the situation becomes increasingly desperate. With limited time, enormous risks, and thousands of lives potentially at stake, Frank and Will demonstrate extraordinary courage and determination in their attempt to stop the disaster. Combining breathtaking train sequences, intense suspense, powerful performances, and nonstop action, the film explores bravery, teamwork, sacrifice, responsibility, and the remarkable courage of ordinary people facing extraordinary circumstances.

🎭 Genre: Action • Thriller • Drama

⭐ IMDb: 6.8/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 38m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Tony Scott

source_details.synopsis: Unstoppable is a 2010 American disaster action thriller film directed and produced by Tony Scott, written by Mark Bomback, and starring Denzel Washington and Chris Pine. It is based on the real-life CSX 8888 incident, telling the story of a runaway freight train and the two men who attempt to stop it. It was the last film Scott directed before his death in 2012. The film was released in the United States on November 12, 2010, by 20th Century Fox. It received generally positive reviews from critics and grossed $167.8 million against a production budget between $85–100 million.
